# srgn - a code surgeon

A `grep`-like tool which understands source code syntax and allows for manipulation in
addition to search.

Like `grep`, regular expressions are a core primitive. Unlike `grep`, additional
capabilities allow for **higher precision**, with **options for manipulation**. This
allows `srgn` to operate along dimensions regular expressions and IDE tooling (*Rename
all*, *Find all references*, ...) alone cannot, complementing them.

`srgn` is organized around *actions* to take (if any), acting only within precise,
optionally **language grammar-aware** *scopes*. In terms of existing tools, think of it
as a mix of `tr`, `sed`, `ripgrep` and `tree-sitter`, with a design goal of
*simplicity*: if you know regex and the basics of the language you are working with, you
are good to go.

## Supported Languages

- C
- C#
- Go
- HCL (Terraform)
- Python
- Rust
- TypeScript

## Quick Usage

The most simple `srgn` usage works similar to `tr`:

```bash
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'
Hello there!
```

Matches for the regular expression pattern (the *scope*) are replaced (the *action*) by
the second positional argument. Zero or more actions can be specified:

```bash
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn '[wW]orld'
Hello World!
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn --upper '[wW]orld' -- 'you'
Hello YOU!
```

### Language-Aware Scoping

`srgn` can scope to syntactical elements of source code. For example, searching only
within Python `class` definitions:

```bash
$ cat birds.py | srgn --python 'class' 'age'
11:    age: int
15:        self.age += 1
```

If standard input is not given, `srgn` finds relevant source files automatically and
processes them recursively at high speed.

### Actions

- **Replacement**: `srgn 'pattern' -- 'replacement'` — replace matches
- **Deletion** (`-d`): remove matched content
- **Squeezing** (`-s`): squeeze repeated matches into single occurrences
- **Uppercasing** (`--upper`): convert matches to uppercase
- **Lowercasing** (`--lower`): convert matches to lowercase
- **Titlecasing** (`--titlecase`): convert matches to title case
- **Normalization** (`--normalize`): Unicode NFD normalization (strip diacritics)
- **Symbols** (`--symbols`/`-S`): replace ASCII symbols with Unicode equivalents
- **German** (`--german`/`-g`): replace German alternative spellings (ae→ä, oe→ö, etc.)

Actions are composable. For example:

```bash
$ echo 'Koeffizienten != Bruecken...' | srgn -Sgu
KOEFFIZIENTEN ≠ BRÜCKEN...
```

### Scopes

- **Regex scope** (first positional argument): narrows processing to matches
- **Language scope** (`--python`, `--rust`, `--go`, `--typescript`, `--csharp`, `--c`, `--hcl`): scope to language constructs like `class`, `comments`, `strings`, `doc-strings`, `imports`, `function`, `struct`, `unsafe`, `attribute`, etc.
- **Literal scope** (`-l`): interpret the scope as a literal string instead of regex
- Multiple language scopes can be combined (AND logic by default, or OR with `-j`)

Dynamic queries use `~` to filter by name: `--go 'struct~[tT]est'` finds only structs
with names matching `[tT]est`.

Custom tree-sitter queries are supported via `--<lang>-query '<S-expression>'`.

### Working with Files

- Without stdin, `srgn` recursively discovers and processes files based on language
- Use `--files` to list which files would be processed
- Use `--files-with-matches` to show files containing matches
- Use `--inplace` to modify files in-place (use with caution)
- Use `--dry-run` to preview changes without applying them
- Use `--sorted` for deterministic output ordering

### Output Format

- In search mode (language scope, no actions): prints matching lines with line numbers
- In replacement mode: prints the full (modified) output
- Use `--only-matching` to print only matched portions
- Use `--line-numbers` to include line numbers
- Use `--count` to print only the count of matches

### Fail Conditions

Control exit codes based on match results:

- `--fail-any`: fail (exit 1) if any match is found
- `--fail-none`: fail (exit 1) if no match is found

### Installation

#### Prebuilt Binaries

Download a prebuilt binary from the
[releases](https://github.com/alexpovel/srgn/releases/latest).

#### Homebrew

```
brew install srgn
```

#### Nix

```
nix-shell -p srgn
```

#### Arch Linux

Available via the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=srgn).

#### MacPorts

```
sudo port install srgn
```

#### Shell Completions

Various shells are supported for shell completion scripts. For example, append
`eval "$(srgn --completions zsh)"` to `~/.zshrc` for completions in ZSH.

### Usage

```
srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLAC

### Output Format

- In search mode (language scope, no actions): prints matching lines with line numbers
- In replacement mode: prints the full (modified) output
- Use `--only-matching` to print only matched portions
- Use `--line-numbers` to include line numbers
- Use `--count` to print only the count of matches

### Fail Conditions

Control exit codes based on match results:

- `--fail-any`: fail (exit 1) if any match is found
- `--fail-none`: fail (exit 1) if no match is found

### Installation

#### Prebuilt Binaries

Download a prebuilt binary from the
[releases](https://github.com/alexpovel/srgn/releases/latest).

#### Homebrew

```
brew install srgn

#### Nix

```
nix-shell -p srgn
```

#### Arch Linux

Available via the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=srgn).

#### MacPorts

```
sudo port install srgn
```

#### Shell Completions

Various shells are supported for shell completion scripts. For example, append
`eval "$(srgn --completions zsh)"` to `~/.zshrc` for completions in ZSH.

```
srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

run(["-s",".+"],"abc\ndef\n")
run(["-s","a+"],"aaaa\n") # single match aaaa so no squeeze?

run(["<.*?>","--","X"],"<a><b>\n")

chars = string.punctuation  # 32

import subprocess, re, shlex
def run(args,inp):
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,text=True)
    err=re.sub(r'\[[^\]]*Z ','[',p.stderr)
    print(f"$ {shlex.join(args)}\ninp={inp!r}\n-> {p.returncode} out={p.stdout!r} err={err!r}\n")

py = '''# a comment
import os
from sys import path
x = "hello string"
y = 'single'
class Bird:
    age: int
    def birthday(self):
        self.age += 1
def greet(name):
    """Docstring here."""
    return f"hi {name}"
'''
run(["--python","class"],py)
run(["--python","class","age"],py)
run(["--python","comments"],py)
run(["--python","strings"],py)
run(["--python","imports"],py)
run(["--python","def"],py)
run(["--python","class","-u","age"],py)
run(["--python","strings","-u"],py)
run(["--python","strings","-u","hello"],py)
run(["--python","strings",".*","--","X"],py)
# Search mode definition: language scope, no action, (?) is regex scope given? default .* if no positional
run(["--python","strings","hello"],py)
# what if no language but stdin and no action = earlier passthrough error
run(["hello"],py)
# language scope with replacement but no regex scope
run(["--python","strings","--","X"],py)

import subprocess, re, shlex, shutil, os, pathlib
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def setup():
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/st", ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs("/tmp/st/sub",exist_ok=True)
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/a.py").write_text('x = "hello"\ny="bye"\n')
    pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/b.py").write_text('z = "hello world"\n')
def run(args, inp=None):
    setup()
    kw=dict(cwd="/tmp/st", capture_output=True, text=True)
    if inp is None: kw['stdin']=subprocess.DEVNULL
    else: kw['input']=inp
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, **kw)
    print(f"$ {shlex.join(args)} inp={inp!r} -> {p.returncode} out={p.stdout!r} err={p.stderr!r}")
# TTY search files
run(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings","hello","--sorted"])
run(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings","hello"])
# TTY action files
run(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings","-u","hello","--sorted"])
print(pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/a.py").read_text())
# TTY dry-run files sorted
run(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings","-u","hello","--sorted","--dry-run"])
run(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--stdout-detection","force-pipe","--python","strings","-u","hello","--sorted","--dry-run"])
# TTY stdin search multiline
run(["--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings"], inp='x="a"\ny="b"\n')
run(["--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","class"], inp='class A:\n    pass\n')
# TTY stdin dry-run
run(["--stdout-detection","force-tty","--dry-run","-u","x"], inp='x y x\nz\n')
# Pipe search when ranges on multiple lines etc
# file action: no change but in-scope
pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/a.py").write_text('x = "HELLO"\n')
def run2(args):
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args,cwd="/tmp/st",stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,capture_output=True,text=True)
    print(f"$ {shlex.join(args)} -> {p.returncode} out={p.stdout!r} err={p.stderr!r}")
setup(); pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/a.py").write_text('x = "HELLO"\n'); pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/b.py").write_text('z = "bye"\n')
run2(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--python","strings","-u","HELLO","--sorted"])
setup(); pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/a.py").write_text('x = "hello"\n'); pathlib.Path("/tmp/st/b.py").write_text('z = "bye"\n')
run2(["--stdin-detection","force-unreadable","--python","strings","hello","--","hello","--sorted"])
# stdin detection with file redirect etc later

import subprocess, os
for term in ["xterm-256color","screen","dumb",None]:
    env=dict(os.environ)
    if term: env["TERM"]=term
    else: env.pop("TERM",None)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--python","strings"], input='x="hi"\n', capture_output=True, env=env)
    print(term, p.stdout)
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--stdout-detection","force-tty","--dry-run","-u","hi"], input='hi\n', capture_output=True, env=env)
    print(" dry", p.stdout)
# analogous with NO_COLOR etc?
PY
# Use a pty to see real tty behaviour
python3 - << 'PY'
import pty, os, subprocess, sys
# run with stdout as pty slave
import os, pty
master, slave = pty.openpty()
p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable","--python","strings"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
os.close(slave)
p.stdin.write(b'x="hi" # c\n'); p.stdin.close()
out=b""
while True:
    try:
        d=os.read(master,1024)
        if not d: break
        out+=d
    except OSError: break
p.wait()
print("pty search out",out)
master, slave = pty.openpty()
p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable","--dry-run","-u","hi"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
os.close(slave)
p.stdin.write(b'hi bye hi\n'); p.stdin.close()
out=b""
while True:
    try:
        d=os.read(master,1024)
        if not d: break
        out+=d
    except OSError: break
p.wait()
print("pty dry out",out)
PY"}

    # brace contexts: classify each '{' as struct/enum/union body, function body, or other block
    # Determine function definitions and declarations first
    funcs=[]  # dict decl_range(name..)), def_range(start..end) or None, name
    # brace depth per token
    depth_arr=[]; d=0
    for t in st:
        if t.text=='{': depth_arr.append(d); d+=1
        elif t.text=='}': d-=1; depth_arr.append(d)
        else: depth_arr.append(d)
    # Find paren groups that are function declarators: ident '(' ... ')' followed by '{' or ';' and at depth0 statement context, name not keyword,
    # and before name there's a return type token in same statement (heuristic).
    for i,t in enumerate(st):
        if t.text!='(' or i==0: continue
        name_idx=i-1
        if st[name_idx].kind!='ident' or st[name_idx].text in _C_KEYWORDS: continue
        if depth_arr[i]!=0 and depth_arr[name_idx]!=0: continue
        # pointer declarators: (*name)(...) - skip for now
        ci=find_matching(st,pairs,i)
        if ci is None: continue
        after=ci+1
        # skip qualifiers (const etc) K&R param decls ignored
        while after<n and st[after].kind=='ident' and st[after].text in ('const','noexcept'): after+=1
        if after<n and st[after].text=='{':
            body_close=find_matching(st,pairs,after)
            # statement start: walk back to previous ';' or '}' or '{' at depth0 or start, skipping preproc tokens (#... handled as punct/idents may pollute; use line boundaries if preprocessor)
            a=name_idx
            # walk back over type tokens to statement boundary
            j=name_idx-1; start=name_idx
            while j>=0 and st[j].text not in (';','}','{'):
                start=j; j-=1
            if body_close is not None:
                funcs.append({'name':st[name_idx].text,'decl':(name_idx,ci),'def':(start,body_close),'proto':False})
        elif after<n and st[after].text==';':
            # prototype only if before name there is at least one type token in statement and depth0
            if depth_arr[name_idx]!=0: continue
            j=name_idx-1; has_type=False; start=name_idx
            while j>=0 and st[j].text not in (';','}','{'):
                has_type=True; start=j; j-=1
            if has_type:
                funcs.append({'name':st[name_idx].text,'decl':(name_idx,ci),'def':None,'proto':True,'decl_stmt':(start,after)})
    if scope=='function-def':
        return [tok_range(st,f['def'][0],f['def'][1]) for f in funcs if f['def']]
    if scope=='function-decl':
        return [tok_range(st,f['decl'][0],f['decl'][1]) for f in funcs]
    # call expressions
    def call_ranges():
        out=[]; decl_parens={f['decl'][0] for f in funcs}
        for i,t in enumerate(st):
            if t.text!='(' or i==0: continue
            # callee end at i-1: ident, or ']' / ')'? simple chains with ./->
            ce=i-1
            if st[ce].kind=='ident' and st[ce].text in _C_KEYWORDS: continue
            if st[ce].kind not in ('ident',) and st[ce].text not in (')',']'): continue
            a=ce
            # walk back over member chain
            while a>=2 and st[a-1].text in ('.','->') and (st[a-2].kind=='ident' or st[a-2].text in (')',']')):
                a=a-2
            if a in decl_parens or ce in decl_parens: continue
            # exclude function declarator: if this '(' belongs to a func decl/def
            if any(f['decl'][0]==a or f['decl'][0]==ce for f in funcs): continue
            ci=find_matching(st,pairs,i)
            if ci is not None: out.append(tok_range(st,a,ci))
        return [r for r in out if r]
    if scope=='call-expression':
        return call_ranges()
    if scope=='function':
        out=[tok_range(st,f['decl'][0],f['decl'][1]) for f in funcs]+call_ranges()
        return merge_ranges(out)

{"command":"cat >> app/srgnpkg/langs.py << 'PY'

# ---------------- C# ----------------
_CS_KEYWORDS={"abstract","as","base","bool","break","byte","case","catch","char","checked","class","const","continue","decimal","default","delegate","do","double","else","enum","event","explicit","extern","false","finally","fixed","float","for","foreach","goto","if","implicit","in","int","interface","internal","is","lock","long","namespace","new","null","object","operator","out","override","params","private","protected","public","readonly","ref","return","sbyte","sealed","short","sizeof","stackalloc","static","string","struct","switch","this","throw","true","try","typeof","uint","ulong","unchecked","unsafe","ushort","using","virtual","void","volatile","while","var","dynamic","record","init","get","set","add","remove","where","when","yield","async","await","nameof","global","partial","required","scoped","file","nint","nuint"}
_CS_MODIFIERS={"public","private","protected","internal","static","abstract","virtual","override","sealed","readonly","extern","unsafe","partial","async","new","const","volatile","file","required"}

def _cs_types(st,pairs):
    types=[]  # kind,a,b,name,body_open,body_close
    n=len(st)
    for i,t in enumerate(st):
        if t.kind=='ident' and t.text in ('class','struct','interface','enum','record'):
            # skip record without following type kw? record class/struct handled at 'class'/'struct'; bare record = record class
            kind=t.text
            # name
            ni=i+1
            if ni>=n or st[ni].kind!='ident': continue
            name=st[ni].text
            # find body '{' or ';'
            j=ni+1; par=br=0; body=None; end=None
            while j<n:
                if st[j].text=='(': par+=1
                elif st[j].text==')': par-=1
                elif st[j].text=='[': br+=1
                elif st[j].text==']': br-=1
                elif st[j].text=='{' and par==0 and br==0:
                    body=j; end=find_matching(st,pairs,j); break
                elif st[j].text==';' and par==0 and br==0:
                    end=j; break
                j+=1
            if end is None: continue
            # start: walk backward over modifiers and attributes to boundary
            a=i
            while a>0:
                prev=st[a-1]
                if prev.text==']':
                    oi=pairs.get(a-1)
                    if oi is not None:
                        a=oi; continue
                    break
                if prev.kind=='ident' and (prev.text in _CS_MODIFIERS or prev.text=='record'):
                    a-=1; continue
                break
            types.append({'kind':kind,'a':a,'b':end,'name':name,'name_idx':ni,'body':body,'kw':i})
    return types

def _cs_member_segments(st,pairs,types):
    """Members inside type bodies: split body (excl nested types handled separately) into segments.
    Each segment: a..b inclusive (b may be matching brace of member body or ';')"""
    members=[]
    type_by_body={t['body']:t for t in types if t['body'] is not None}
    for tp in types:
        if tp['body'] is None: continue
        bo=tp['body']; bc=tp['b']
        i=bo+1
        while i<bc:
            # skip nested type declarations as one segment and mark
            a=i; par=br=0; j=i; end=None
            while j<bc:
                tt=st[j]
                if tt.text=='(' : par+=1
                elif tt.text==')': par-=1
                elif tt.text=='[': br+=1
                elif tt.text==']': br-=1
                elif tt.text=='{' and par==0 and br==0:
                    ci=find_matching(st,pairs,j); end=ci; break
                elif tt.text==';' and par==0 and br==0:
                    # but semicolons in for loops happen inside method bodies only (inside braces handled), at member level ends member, unless part of '= ... =>'? still end
                    end=j; break
                j+=1
            if end is None: break
            # expression-bodied members with '{' in initializer: e.g. field with object init {..}; If segment contains '=' before '{' and no '(' header directly preceding, it might end at following ';'
            # Keep simple: if end token brace and next is ';' and segment contains '=' and doesn't look like method/property (no get/set right after '{'), extend to ';'
            members.append({'a':a,'b':end,'type':tp})
            i=end+1
    return members
PY

import subprocess, re, os, shutil, pathlib, sys
REF="/workspace/executable"; OUR="/tmp/our_exe"
def norm(s):
    s=re.sub(r'\[\d{4}[^\]]*Z ','[TS ',s)
    s=s.replace('/tmp/df_ref','/TMP').replace('/tmp/df_our','/TMP')
    return s
def setup(root):
    shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root+"/sub")
    pathlib.Path(root,"a.py").write_text('x = "hello"\n# hello comment\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,"b.py").write_text('y = "bye"\nz = "hello world"\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,"sub/c.py").write_text('class A:\n    s="hello"\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,"d.rs").write_text('fn main(){ println!("hello"); } // hi\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,"e.txt").write_text('hello text\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,".hidden.py").write_text('h="hello"\n')
    pathlib.Path(root,"sub/f.txt").write_text('hello again\n')
def snapshot(root):
    result={}
    for p in sorted(pathlib.Path(root).rglob("*")):
        if p.is_file(): result[str(p.relative_to(root))]=p.read_bytes()
    return result
def run_case(args, sorted_stdout=False):
    setup("/tmp/df_ref"); setup("/tmp/df_our")
    pr=subprocess.run([REF]+args,cwd="/tmp/df_ref",stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,capture_output=True,text=True)
    po=subprocess.run([OUR]+args,cwd="/tmp/df_our",stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,capture_output=True,text=True)
    rr=(pr.returncode, pr.stdout, norm(pr.stderr), snapshot("/tmp/df_ref"))
    oo=(po.returncode, po.stdout, norm(po.stderr), snapshot("/tmp/df_our"))
    # for unsorted searches/actions whose stdout order can differ, compare sorted lines if flag in args? Caller decides separately
    if rr!=oo:
        print(f"\nFAIL {args}\nREF rc={rr[0]} out={rr[1]!r} err={rr[2]!r}\n files={rr[3]}\nOUR rc={oo[0]} out={oo[1]!r} err={oo[2]!r}\n files={oo[3]}")
        return False
    print(f"OK {args}")
    return True

        """Return captured ranges for expression, constrained to context ranges if given (containment)."""
        kind,val=expr
        captures=[]
        if kind=='atom':
            return captures
        if kind=='captured':
            child,caps=val
            return eval_expr(child,context_ranges)+node_ranges_of(child,context_ranges)
        if kind=='alt':
            for sub in val:
                captures.extend(eval_expr(sub,context_ranges))
            return captures
        # list: pattern
        items=val

        if head[0]=='atom' and head[1].startswith('#'):
            return captures  # predicates handled at parent level

        if head[0]=='atom' and head[1]!='_':

        for sub in items[1:]:

def _hcl_lex(text):
    toks=[]; i=0; n=len(text)
    while i<n:
        c=text[i]
        if c=='\n': toks.append(Tok('nl',c,i,i+1)); i+=1; continue
        if c in ' \t\r': i+=1; continue
        if text.startswith('//',i) or c=='#':
            j=text.find('\n',i); j=n if j==-1 else j
            toks.append(Tok('comment',text[i:j],i,j)); i=j; continue
        if text.startswith('/*',i):
            j=text.find('*/',i+2); j=n if j==-1 else j+2
            toks.append(Tok('comment',text[i:j],i,j)); i=j; continue
        if text.startswith('<<',i):
            m=re.match(r'<<-?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\r?\n',text[i:])
            if m:
                marker=m.group(1); start_content=i+m.end()
                # find line with marker alone (allow indent)
                mm=re.search(r'(?m)^[ \t]*'+re.escape(marker)+r'[ \t]*(\r?\n|$)',text[start_content:])
                if mm:
                    content_end=start_content+mm.start(); end=start_content+mm.end()
                    # marker line content excluded; frag from after first newline to start of marker line; rough interpolation ignored
                    toks.append(Tok('string',text[i:end],i,end,frags=[(start_content,content_end)] if content_end>start_content else [],quote='heredoc')); i=end; continue
        if c=='"':
            end=_scan_quoted(text,i,'"',allow_newline=False)
            content=text[i+1:end-1] if end>i and text[end-1:end]=='"' else text[i+1:end]
            # fragments excluding ${...} and %{...}
            frags=[]; cur=0; k=0
            while k<len(content):
                if content.startswith('$${',k) or content.startswith('%%{',k): k+=3; continue
                if content.startswith('${',k) or content.startswith('%{',k):

    verb=args.vals.get('verbose',0)
    if base+verb>5:
        sys.stderr.write("Requested additional verbosity on top of env default exceeds maximum, will use maximum\\n")

'''
